summary: Ram Shankar Tripathi (1929–2019) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was Head of Buddhist Philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Dean of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and taught at Banaras Hindu and Pune universities.

Ram Sharan Sharma (1919–2011) was a historian and Indologist who studied at Patna University and SOAS under Wilhelm Rau and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held professorships at Patna University and Delhi University, and founded the Indian Council of Historical Research.

Rama Kant Agnihotri is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at York University from 1973 to 1975, earning a DPhil in 1979, and served on an editorial board at the University of Delhi from 1980 to 2010.

Rama Mishra Shastri (1854–1911) was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he was attested as a professor between 1882 and 1889 and as an assistant professor of Sāṅkhya in 1914.

Rama Nath Sharma (b. 1939) is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raghunatha Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi, completing his PhD at Rochester. He taught at Allahabad and Rochester, becoming a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1976.

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar (1837–1925) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug, earning degrees from Mumbai and Göttingen. He served as professor at Elphinstone College and Deccan College, and became Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai in 1893.

Ramanath Pandey is an Indologist who completed his BA at the University of Delhi and PhD at Ranchi University. He worked at the University of Delhi, Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, and became a professor at Parshwanath Vidyapeeth in 2025.

Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indologist who worked in the Sādhulāla research department at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944) and served as Head of the Veda Department at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (attested 1970).

Ramaprasad Chanda (1873–1942) worked in archaeology, history, and Indology after studying at Scottish Church College. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India, lectured at the University of Calcutta, and was Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum, Kolkata.
Ramaprasada Tripathi was an Indologist and linguist who taught Rama Nath Sharma and held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he served as vice-chancellor (attested 1976 and 2001).

Ramaranjan Mukherji (1928–2010) was an Indologist who earned his BA and PhD at Calcutta and a DLitt at Jadavpur. He headed Sanskrit at Jadavpur and served as vice chancellor of the University of Burdwan and Rabindra Bharati University.
Ramashastri Bhagavatacharya was an Indologist attested in 1891 as an assistant professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as a teacher at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi.

Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith, L. D. Arts College (attested 1938), and S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women (attested 1938).

Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar (1909–2001) was an Indologist who earned degrees at Mumbai and Heidelberg. He served as professor and dean at Savitribai Phule Pune University and was Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 1939 to 2001.
Ramdas Lamb (b. 1945) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He holds a post as affiliate faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, where his affiliation is attested in 2005 and 2026.

Ramesh Chandra Negi (b. 1956) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has worked at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, serving as a research assistant (attested 2001–2004) and associate professor (attested 2026).

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar (1888–1980) was a historian and Indologist educated at Presidency University and Calcutta. He served as professor and provost at the University of Dhaka, held principal posts at BHU and Nagpur, and was president of The Asiatic Society.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1967, he headed the Department of History and Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and held visiting lectureships in the United States.

Ramin Etesami is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Lozang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).

Ramkrishna Bhattacharya (1947–2022) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Calcutta under Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya. He taught at Ananda Mohan College and retired as a professor of English from the University of Calcutta.
